source.title: Optimized Weight Initialization on the Stiefel Manifold for Deep ReLU Neural Networks
source.authors: Hyungu Lee; Taehyeong Kim; Hayoung Choi

record.tranche_reason: The paper compares weight initializations across network depths and reports classification performance, testing whether initialization affects depth stability. It uses a new initialization and test accuracy rather than the original studies’ specific methods or training-error measure.
record.gate_note: The paper reports test accuracy, not training classification error, so the results do not directly establish whether the networks reached zero or near-zero training error. Its theoretical claims about signal and gradient propagation are not separate empirical results. The reported MNIST alignment correlation (r = 0.8178) is an empirical motivation for the method, but does not measure the claim’s training-error outcome.
record.test_reason: The initialization-by-depth comparisons bear on V4's trainable-depth component: changing initialization allows otherwise identical plain ReLU networks to retain useful predictive performance at depths where other initializations collapse. Test accuracy provides indirect evidence of trainability; it does not establish training speed, training error, or the proposed gradient mechanism.
record.authors_conclusion: The record's paraphrase is accurate for the depth experiments and ablation. The authors conclude that their mean-aligned semi-orthogonal initialization maintains deep-network predictive performance, with mean calibration providing the primary protection against collapse and semi-orthogonality adding an accuracy benefit. Their broader conclusion also emphasizes few-shot advantages and sensitivity to input mean shift on tabular tasks. Empirical outcomes are test accuracy and regression RMSE; signal and gradient explanations come from initialization-time theoretical analysis rather than measured training trajectories.
record.recipe_differences: Introduces a new semi-orthogonal, all-ones-aligned initialization. Experiments use fully connected ReLU networks, Adam, cross-entropy, and test accuracy; the paper does not directly measure training error or initialization-specific training speed.
record.method_sensitivity: Depth, dataset, initialization scheme, and activation choice. Tabular experiments also report performance changing with the input mean-shift parameter α0.

fits_no_version.finding: Section 3.1 reports a correlation of r = 0.8178 between middle-layer all-ones alignment and one-shot MNIST test accuracy in a 784→64→64→10 network.
fits_no_version.proposed_claim: Initialization alignment predicts few-shot generalization in this fixed shallow architecture; this correlation alone does not measure learning speed or trainable depth.

record.problems: The empirical depth experiments report test accuracy rather than training classification error. The main comparisons are on MNIST and Fashion-MNIST, not CIFAR-10 or CIFAR-100. The test set results do not directly show whether training error reached zero or near zero.
record.rows_left_out: The remaining Table 1 depth entries, including depths 10, 20, 30, 40, 60, 70, 80, and 90, were omitted to stay within the 60-row limit; Table 1 reports these separately for each initialization and dataset. The activation-family results in Table 3, few-shot results in Table 4, and tabular results in Table 6 were also omitted because those settings are outside V4’s named initialization-speed and trainable-depth outcome. Their results report test accuracy or regression RMSE, not training error or training speed.

untested.parts: Near-zero training classification error in sufficiently large convolutional networks on CIFAR-10/CIFAR-100, including corrupted or random labels.
Teacher-student ReLU problems, spurious-local-minimum frequencies, and the effect of one or two extra student neurons.
Training-error degradation in plain batch-normalized convolutional networks, identity-shortcut comparisons, deep tanh exceptions, and Fixup.

Learning speed and convergence trajectories; direct empirical signal and gradient propagation; orthogonal versus equal-variance Gaussian initialization in very deep tanh networks; convolutional kernels and 10,000-layer training. The depth experiments also change the learning rate with depth, so they do not isolate depth under a fixed learning rate.
Above-threshold learning rates, transient loss increases, curvature reduction, edge-of-stability dynamics, and divergence thresholds.
Batch normalization versus no normalization, higher-learning-rate tolerance, and Fixup's speed and stability.

record.verdict_notes: States describe useful learning and depth stability within each initialization condition; V4's initialization effect is assessed through comparisons, so failed controls can support it. Xavier's ReLU failures do not challenge an activation-matched initialization claim, and orthogonal ReLU failures do not challenge the tanh-specific clause. Tables 3, 4 and 6 also bear on initialization-dependent depth performance, but their omission is already declared in rows_left_out. No challenge verdict is warranted from these results.

versions.untested_parts: Training classification error, CIFAR-10/CIFAR-100, and corrupted or random labels are not reported.
No two-layer teacher-student problem, spurious-minimum rate, or student-width sweep is tested.
No plain-versus-residual shortcut comparison is reported.

The study tests a new ReLU initialization on fully connected networks using test accuracy. It does not test the named initialization methods’ training speeds or gradient-flow claims, very deep tanh networks, orthogonal convolution kernels, or 10,000-layer networks.
No learning-rate stability threshold, loss rise, curvature or sharpness measurement, or above-threshold learning-rate sweep is reported.

relationships.condition: Plain width-64 ReLU networks on full MNIST and Fashion-MNIST, depths 50 and 100, Adam for 100 epochs with depth-scaled learning rates
relationships.reason: r1-r4 and r17-r20 retain approximately 96–97% MNIST or 87–88% Fashion-MNIST accuracy, while r16, r28, r30-r32 collapse at the same tested depths; this supports initialization-dependent trainable depth through predictive-performance evidence.
relationships.display_finding: The proposed initialization retained approximately 96–97% MNIST and 87–88% Fashion-MNIST accuracy, while comparison initializations collapsed at the same depths.

source_check.label: supports
source_check.condition: Plain width-64 ReLU networks on full MNIST and Fashion-MNIST, depths 50 and 100, Adam for 100 epochs with depth-scaled learning rates
source_check.reason: Table 1 confirms useful deep-network performance in r1-r4 and r17-r20 alongside collapse in r16, r28 and r30-r32, supporting initialization-dependent trainable depth through predictive-performance evidence.

relationships.condition: Mean calibration ablation in plain ReLU networks on both datasets at depths 50 and 100
relationships.reason: r35-r36 and r41-r42 retain useful performance without semi-orthogonality, while r13-r14 and r29-r30 deteriorate without mean alignment; the comparisons support activation-sensitive initialization, with an additional accuracy benefit from semi-orthogonality in r1-r2 and r17-r18.
relationships.display_finding: Useful performance persisted without semi-orthogonality but deteriorated without mean alignment, while adding semi-orthogonality improved accuracy further.

source_check.label: supports
source_check.condition: Mean calibration ablation in plain ReLU networks on both datasets at depths 50 and 100
source_check.reason: Table 2 and Section 6.2 confirm that r35-r36 and r41-r42 retain useful performance without semi-orthogonality, whereas r13-r14 and r29-r30 deteriorate; r1-r2 and r17-r18 show the additional accuracy benefit of the combined initialization.

relationships.condition: He initialization in narrow plain ReLU networks as depth increases
relationships.reason: r9-r10 and r25-r26 retain useful learning but progressively lose test accuracy with depth, showing that ReLU variance matching alone does not ensure depth-stable predictive performance in this recipe; the evidence does not isolate training error.
relationships.display_finding: Useful learning persisted, but test accuracy progressively decreased with depth; the evidence did not isolate training error.

source_check.condition: He initialization in narrow plain ReLU networks as depth increases
source_check.reason: Table 1 confirms progressively declining He test accuracy in r9-r10 and r25-r26. This qualifies the sufficiency of ReLU variance matching for depth-stable predictive performance in this recipe; it does not challenge the tanh comparison or establish a training-speed deficit.
